Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. Our procurement team has a short questionnaire focused on SLO measurement and monitoring for uptime/latency. They need concrete answers to verify we can rely on your commitments and to understand the exception/approval path. Can you provide the following details?

- How do you measure request latency (aggregation window, percentiles, which endpoints are included)?
- What is the defined success metric (error classes counted as failures)?
- Sampling / ingestion policy for metrics and traces (any downsampling?)
- Alerting thresholds (e.g., p95 > X ms, 5xx rate > Y%) and who gets paged
- Retention period for metric granularity (raw vs aggregated)
- Customer access: can we get read-only dashboards / query access? Typical ask is a Grafana link + example queries
- Exception handling: if we need a temporary SLO adjustment during on-boarding or load spikes, what is the approval workflow and typical turnaround?
- Audit logs and evidence for compliance reviews (exportable PDFs / CSVs?)

I've attached the procurement questionnaire (ACME_procurement_SLO_questions.pdf). We need answers by Friday so the security/procurement group can clear the risk. If you prefer a short call, tell me availability.

Best,
James

Acme Corporation

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: needed telemetry details for SLA review

James,

Appreciate the clear list — below is a concise plan and the artifacts we can provide. Attaching a short SLO measurement spec and a temporary Grafana invite template. We can also do a 30-min walkthrough if you want to step through the dashboards.

Summary (high level)
- Latency measurement: per-request end-to-end server processing time measured at the inference gateway (time from request arrival to last token emitted). We record percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) over 1m and 5m windows; procurement usually uses p95 over a 5 minute sliding window for commitments.
- Success metric: request considered failed on any 5xx response or 429 (rate limit) returned to the client; client-side timeouts are not included unless they surface as gateway 504.
- Aggregation & sampling: we ingest full-count metrics for all requests for 30 days at 1s resolution, then roll up to 1m granularity for 90 days. Traces are sampled (1-5% by default) but we can increase sampling for onboarding windows.
- Alerts & escalation: standard alert example — p95(latency) > 350ms for 5 consecutive mins => PagerDuty P1 to SRE; error rate (5xx) > 1.5% sustained for 10 mins => pager to support + account CS. We will share the actual alert rules.
- Retention: metrics raw (1s) 30d, aggregated (1m) 90d, long-term aggregates (daily) 13 months. Audit logs (API access, config changes) retained 24 months.
- Customer access: we can provide time-bound, read-only Grafana links scoped to your account (IP allowlist + token expiry). We also support CSV/JSON exports of query results and ad-hoc metric snapshots for procurement evidence.
- SLO exceptions: To request a temporary SLO adjustment, submit the form to compliance@redwood.ai (or through the shared Drive doc). Approval route: Account owner -> Technical review (SRE) -> Compliance. Typical turnaround: 24-72 business hours depending on scope. Exceptions > 14 days require exec approval and documented mitigation.

Artifacts and next steps:
- Attached: redwood-slo-measurement-spec.pdf (detailed definitions and example queries)
- We'll create a read-only Grafana link for your security team; if you prefer an IP allowlist, share the IPs and TTL. Template invite: grafana-temp-invite.txt (contains steps and TTL options).
- Marissa will send the alerting rule excerpt and sample dashboard.
- If you want raw metric exports for the period you specify, Ethan can produce a snapshot.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/Procurement/Acme-SLO-Responses-2026-08-24 (contains templates + sample alert rules)
HubSpot deal: deal_9883721

I'll loop in engineering to confirm the export window and retention details. Want to confirm: do you need a 14-day backfill or something longer for the procurement review?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Jordan — confirmed. Details below (technical):

- Retention: metrics ingest at 1s resolution stored for 30 days; we automatically roll to 1m resolution and keep those for 90 days. We also generate daily aggregates retained 13 months. Audit logs kept 24 months.
- Backfill/export: we can produce a 14-day export of the full metric stream (CSV/NDJSON) covering the account namespace. For very large windows we may need to stage the export; 14 days is fine and we can deliver within 48 hours of request. Sample export filename: slo-snapshot-20260824.ndjson (attached as stub).
- Traces: sampling adjustable via feature flag per account; increasing from 2% -> 20% for a two-week period is low-risk and we can enable on request.
- Alert rules: the alerting policy Jordan outlined maps to our PagerDuty escalation paths. Marissa has the alert snippets and will attach them to the Drive doc.

I will prepare the export once procurement confirms the period and the email address to deliver to.

—Ethan
